title: Syllogism
note: Statements and conclusions verbatim, typos included ("studends", "conculsion", "conlusion", "conlcusion", "Statemens", "Some potatoes the chips", "Some tables are desktops" in Q53 beside "tablets"). Numbering is normalised: statements 1., 2., 3. and conclusions I., II., III. (the book mixes I./1./A./(A)); Q77 keeps 1. and 2. because its options name them so. Q11 prints no conclusions: its options are the conclusions. Q74 prints options A and B without numerals, alike. Q78 prints its options in the order B, A, C, D; stored by label. Q82 prints both conclusions as "I."; the second is II. The direction covers Q1-97, but the photos stop at Q94's first statement (page 69 begins Chapter 18): Q94-97 are not transcribed.

directions.text: In the following questions below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follows the given statements.
